motion.name: story-relight

motion.name: label-scramble

motion.name: scene-fade-in
motion.purpose: WebGL hero fading in over the SVG poster after its first frame.

motion.name: route-cycle
motion.purpose: Hero scene loop alternating a verified run with a failed probe that rolls back.

motion.name: hero-camera-entrance
motion.purpose: Perspective camera swinging from the poster's straight-on framing to a low rake along the track toward the signal ("route opening"); rake fitted per resize, 12°–38° by stage aspect.

motion.name: hero-camera-follow
motion.purpose: Camera trucks along the track after the route light's leading point (lamps, probe pulse, signal); no ambient drift.

motion.name: lamp-blend
motion.purpose: Scene lamps, lock and points blade blend off → on through a darker amber, green or red, never an olive grey.

motion.name: story-scroll-light
motion.value: animation-timeline: --story-N (view timelines), range: cover 50vh → cover 100% − 50vh, linear
motion.purpose: Amber travels along the story stage's track (stroke-dashoffset) while a step crosses the viewport centre line; IntersectionObserver stepping is the fallback.

motion.name: points-throw
motion.purpose: Fast throw with a small overshoot for the points and the MFA lock.

motionContract: Poster first paint; the hero camera starts at the poster's framing.
One entrance (hero camera rake), then motion only follows the route light or the scroll.
Lazy, gated 3D (loaded + idle, on screen, motion allowed, WebGL2); no post-processing.
Glow on lamps only; depth fog toward the frame; HTML labels projected onto their lamps.
Reduced motion never requests the scene, disposes a running one and keeps the story static.
No scroll-driven animations: the story steps its lit track on the IntersectionObserver.
Off-screen and hidden-tab pause; dispose on pagehide.
DPR 1 on coarse pointers or under 768px, otherwise at most 1.5.

narrative.northStar: "La Cabina de Enclavamiento" (the interlocking signal box)
narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "La Cabina de Enclavamiento" (the interlocking signal box)**

MCM is drawn as a signal box at night. In an interlocking, a route cannot clear until every lever and point along it is proven, and that is how MCM treats a configuration change. Review, MFA, apply and probe light lamp by lamp along a track. The route then holds green (verified) or falls back to the previous one (rolled back). The page is the frame of the box: near-black ground, enamel lever plates with engraved condensed capitals, hairline track diagrams as the structural line, and lamps that light only when something is true.

The tone is a control room, cinematic and precise. It is dark because a signal box works in the dark, so the lamps are the brightest things in the room. Density is low and every section reads like a panel of the frame: a track rule under the heading, the content set out along it. Nothing is a card and nothing is glass. Real captures of the running app are the only imagery.

Motion and 3D are part of the world, and they are allowed freely, with one condition: they report a state. The hero runs the route as a live WebGL scene, and the story section relights the same route as you scroll. Every animated surface has a static twin, so the page reads the same with motion off, without WebGL and before any script runs. `/system` (linked from the footer as "Brand system") is the living storybook: every token, component and state on this page is rendered there from the same source.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black frame ground with enamel text and plates. There are no gradients on surfaces and no glass.
Lamps carry meaning: amber means a route is set (or caution, or rolled back), green means verified, red means failed.
Big Shoulders engraved capitals for display and plates, Overpass for reading, Overpass Mono for commands, data and diagram labels.
Hairline track rules and route diagrams are the structure. Sections never sit in cards, and no label sits above a heading.
One route geometry (`site/src/scripts/route-geometry.ts`) drives the SVG poster, the WebGL scene, the hero labels and the story stage.
Motion is free, but it always reports a state and always has a poster, reduced-motion and no-WebGL equivalent.

rules.name: The Proven Green Rule
rules.body: Green appears only where a change has been verified. It is never a "success" accent, a CTA colour or decoration. If nothing was verified, nothing is green.

rules.name: The Red Means Failed Rule
rules.body: Red appears only for a failed apply or probe. It never signals emphasis, deletion or a warning. Use `danger-text` for any red text under 24px.

rules.name: The Amber Route Rule
rules.body: Amber says "a route is set": the lit track, a caution that applies before you act, and the route back after a rollback. It is never a generic highlight.

rules.name: The Colour Is Never Alone Rule
rules.body: Every lamp state also has a word: StatusLamp always renders its label, pending is a hollow ring, and the diagram labels say Verified, Failed or Rolled back.

rules.name: The Engraved Plate Rule
rules.body: Big Shoulders capitals are for things engraved on the frame: the claim, section names, levers, plates and step labels. Running text is never set in capitals.

rules.name: The Instrument Rule
rules.body: Mono is for commands, code, file names, tabular data and diagram labels only. It is never a costume to make prose look technical.

rules.name: The No Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: No kicker or label sits above a heading. The heading carries its own weight, and the TrackSection rule beneath it does the framing.

rules.name: The Lamps Carry Light Rule
rules.body: Only a lit lamp glows. Nothing else on the page emits light or casts a shadow.

dos: **Do** use green only for verified, red only for failed, and amber for a set route, a caution or a rollback.
**Do** give every lamp colour a word next to it (StatusLamp label, diagram label).
**Do** draw any route diagram from `route-geometry.ts` inside a `.route-rail`, so the poster, labels and scene stay aligned.
**Do** give every animated or 3D surface a poster first paint, a reduced-motion frame, a no-WebGL fallback, a pause control, an off-screen pause and a DPR cap.
**Do** open sections with a TrackSection and keep running text at 68–72ch or narrower.

**Do** theme the browser surfaces from the palette: amber selection, amber caret, enamel-muted on frame scrollbar, 2px enamel-bright focus ring, 4px underline offset, tabular numerals for numbers that line up.
**Do** add every new component or state to `/system` in the same change.
**Do** use only real captures of the running app as imagery, with their alt text and intrinsic size.
donts: **Don't** put a kicker or eyebrow label above a heading.
**Don't** wrap sections or columns in cards, nest a box in a box, or use glass, blur or surface gradients.
**Don't** use green, red or amber as decoration, emphasis or a brand accent.
**Don't** set red text under 24px in `danger`; use `danger-text`. Never set text in `lever-blue`.
**Don't** animate anything that does not report a state, or ship an animation without its static twin.
**Don't** draw message traffic, packets or anything else MCM does not route. The scene shows the change route only.
**Don't** use mono for prose, or Big Shoulders capitals for running text.
**Don't** add drop shadows or hard offset shadows. Depth is the bevel on plates and the light of lamps.
**Don't** use the Eclipse or Mosquitto logos or their motifs. The mark is MCM's own.
